ActiveRun.description: A run in flight on this hub (initiator side).

suite_id.description: Suite id when part of a suite.

suite_index.description: This item's 0-based index in its suite.

suite_profile.description:
The suite's profile (`smoke`, `standard`, `full`, `nightly`) when
part of a suite, so a reloaded UI can follow it.

AppError.description:
An engine error: a stable code plus a human-readable message.

`Display` prints only the message; use [`AppError::code`] to branch.

BenchPeer.description: A same-app peer as the app shows it.

device_name.description: Device name (falls back to the display name).

hello_error.description: Why the last hello failed, if it did.

id.description: Tailscale stable node id: the only peer key used for runs.

same_host.description:
Same machine as this hub, from the host fingerprint in the peer's
hello (§7.4; [`same_host_verdict`](crate::env::same_host_verdict)):
`None` when unknown (no hello yet, a peer that does not admit us and
so withholds its fingerprint, or weak fingerprints that cannot tell).

same_login.description: Same real account as this hub ([`same_login`]).

tagged.description: The peer is a tagged device.

Better.description: Which direction of a summary value is better.

BuildProfile.description:
Rust build profile of one side.

`unknown` only appears in imported v1 reports, which recorded nothing.

ClockInfo.description: Clock offsets taken before and after a run (`network.clock`).

uncertainty_ns.description: The larger uncertainty of the two, ns.

delay_ns.description: δ: round-trip delay of the chosen sample, ns.

t1_ns.description: Initiator `now_ns()` at send (informational; the initiator keeps its own stamp).

Direction.description: tcp / quic direction, seen from the initiator.

Distribution.description:
Summary statistics of a sample set (§7.4).

`samples` counts every sample including lost ones. Percentiles are
nearest-rank over all samples with lost ones ranked as +∞; a percentile is
`None` below its minimum sample count or when it lands on a lost sample.
`min`, `mean`, `max` and `stddev` cover the received samples only.

stddev.description: Sample standard deviation (n − 1) of received values; n ≥ 2.

EgressResults.description:
`RunReport.results` of an `egress` run: the tcp throughput results plus
the route.

bridges.description: Rust loopback bridges on the data path: 1 (tcp has 2).

foreign_dropped.description: Foreign connections and bad headers the sink dropped.

goodput_bytes.description: Payload bytes inside the measurement window.

received_bytes.description: Same as `bytes_total` (the §12 `received ≤ sent` check reads it).

receiver.description: The receiver's accounting (receiver timebase) for one-way runs.

window_ms.description: Length of the measurement window, ms.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable error codes. Serialised in kebab-case (`peer-not-found`, …), so the
app and the control protocol can branch on them.

oneOf.description: The hub (or its node) is not running.
No peer matches the reference, or the sender of a request is unknown.
The peer reference matches more than one peer.
The peer is known but offline or gone.
The responder's admission rule refused this peer (§6 rule 1).
The responder is initiating its own run (§6 rule 3).
This hub is being measured by a peer and cannot start a run (§6 rule 3).
The peer speaks a different control-protocol version.
The peer does not offer the requested workload.
Parameters are out of bounds or malformed; never clamped.
Another process holds this hub's state directory.
No sidecar binary could be found (§5.3).
The run or suite was cancelled.

ack_ok.description: The sender read the receiver's ACK byte.

negotiate_ms.description: OFFER sent → data stream open, ms.

ok.description:
Sent, received and verified (a missing ACK is fine when the
receiver's SHA-256 matches).

sha256_match.description: The receiver's SHA-256 equals the sender's; `None` when unknown.

t_ms.description: When it ended, ms since the run started.

transfer_ms.description: First write to the data stream → ACK read, ms.

ack_failures.description: Iterations whose ACK was not read (valid by SHA-256, untimed).

source_write_ms.description: Writing the source file before the first iteration, ms.

max_overlapping_runs.description: Other runs that shared the responder's hub during this one.

FinishReq.description: `finish`: the initiator is done; collect the responder's numbers.

FtDoneMsg.description: `ft.done`: the responder saw a file-transfer iteration end (no reply).

healthy.description: Whether the network is fully operational.

HelloAck.description: `hello.ack`: who I am, as far as you may know. Always answered, across accounts.

hello.description: The responder's hello (`host_fingerprint` omitted unless admitted).

attempts.description: Measured requests (started after the warmup, before the end).

goodput_mbps.description: Body goodput over the measured window, Mb/s.

latency_ms.description: Latency of measured 2xx answers, ms (timeouts ranked as lost).

port.description: The tailnet port requests went to.

samples_ms.description:
Raw 2xx latencies, ms, ascending; at most 4000 evenly spaced order
statistics when there were more.

server.description: What the responder's server saw (warmup included).

warmup_requests.description: Requests started during the warmup (not counted).

HttpServerStats.description: `finish.ack.stats`: what the responder's server saw (warmup included).

bad_request.description: 400 answers (size above `response_bytes`, or a malformed request).

connections.description: Connections accepted (from the proxy on loopback, or from the tailnet).

forbidden.description: 403 answers (`Tailscale-Node-Id` missing or not the initiator's).

foreign_dropped.description: Tailnet connections dropped by rule 5 (direct target).

HubEvent.description: Events a hub broadcasts (`bench://event` in the app).

oneOf.description:
The node's lifecycle state changed (boxed: it is by far the largest
variant; serialises flat, `{"type": "node", ...NodeState}`).
The peer list changed (debounced to 250 ms).
A peer's run against this hub changed state.

skipped.description: Files that were not reports, could not be normalised, or were already stored.

LocalInfo.description: What this hub knows about itself once running.

app_id.description: The truffle app id (`truffle-bench`, or a per-run id in `pair`).

tailnet.description: Tailnet name, derived from `dns_name` (everything after the first label).

NetworkInfo.description: `network` of a report: where the bytes went.

clock.description: Clock offsets, for workloads that map peer time.

loaded_rtt_ms.description: RTT under load, from the path sampler.

path_bytes.description: Sum of both sides' usermetrics byte deltas.

path_label.description: The verdict (History filters on this, never on `before.connection`).

path_timeline.description: 2 Hz path samples during time-based runs.

settle_ms.description: Path settle time before the run.

topology.description: Same process, same host, or separate hosts.

NodeEnv.description: The environment of one side of a run.

app_foreground_pct.description: App only: share of the run with the window in front, 0–100.

host_fingerprint_weak.description: The fingerprint fell back to the hostname.

tool.description:
`truffle-bench-app`, `truffle-bench-cli`, or for imports the source
tool (`truffle-bench v1`, `truffle-bench v2`, `tsnet-bench`).

since_ms.description: When the hub entered this state, Unix ms.

tailscale_hostname.description: The Tailscale hostname this hub registers as (known before login).

oneOf.description: The node waits for an interactive login (`auth_url` is set).

The tailnet has device approval on and an admin has not approved this
device (`tailscale_hostname`) yet. The node keeps waiting and runs as
soon as it is approved in the Tailscale admin console (Machines).
Every sidecar reports it (`tsnet:needsApproval`, since RFC 008 phase
2); cores before `NodeBuilder::on_network_status` dropped the event,
so hubs built on them stay in `needs-login` or `starting` instead.
The node is up; `local` is set.

OneWayDirection.description: udp / egress direction, seen from the initiator.

oneOf.description: Fragments spread over the frame interval.

PathBytes.description: Bytes per path class, from usermetrics deltas.

oneOf.description: Relayed (DERP or peer relay) the whole run.
Both, or a transition during the run.
No usermetrics and no usable path samples.

t_ms.description: When it was sent, ms since the run started.

discovery_ms.description: Running → this peer first listed, ms.

first_rtt_ms.description: RTT of sample 0 (first contact after settling).

rtt_ms.description: RTT distribution of samples 1… (lost ones ranked as +∞).

ws_connect_ms.description: First `hello` while the peer was not ws_connected → `hello.ack`, ms.

PathSnapshot.description: One ping's view of the path.

connection.description: Connection label; `None` when the ping failed or timed out.

PathTransition.description: A change of connection between consecutive answered pings.

i.description: Index of the first ping on the new connection.

t_ms.description: Its send time, ms since the run started.

PeerHello.description: What a hub says about itself in `hello` / `hello.ack`.

accepts_runs_from_you.description: Whether the asking peer passes this hub's admission rule.

busy.description: Set while this hub is in a data-plane run, e.g. "measuring studio · tcp".

host_fingerprint.description: §7.4 host fingerprint; omitted for peers that are not admitted.

host_fingerprint_weak.description: The fingerprint fell back to the hostname.

workloads.description: Workloads this hub can respond to.

PeerProbe.description: `peer_probe`: a peer, its fresh hello and a path snapshot.

oneOf.description: Data is flowing but not yet measured.
Waiting for in-flight data after the senders stop.

overlapping_runs.description: Other runs active on the responder's hub right now.

params.description: Params as validated and used by the responder.

run_tag.description: 64 random bits chosen by the responder.

params.description: Params; validated again by the responder.

Live values. Receiver-side keys come only from `tick`s; sender-side
keys are distinct (`sent_mbps`).

bytes_total.description: Every payload byte received, warmup included.

download_mbps.description: Download goodput over the overlap window (bidirectional only).

flow_control_ceiling_mbps.description: What quinn's default windows allow at the settled RTT, Mb/s.

The receiver of the measured direction (bidirectional: upload), in

upload_mbps.description: Upload goodput over the overlap window (bidirectional only).

window_bytes.description: Payload bytes inside the measurement window.

The receiver's accounting for one direction of a run, as sent in
`finish.ack.stats` (§8.1). `epoch_ns`/`last_ns` are 0 when nothing arrived.

buckets.description: Payload bytes read in `[epoch + 250·i ms, epoch + 250·(i+1) ms)`.

epoch_ns.description: Receiver `now_ns()` at the first payload byte of any stream.

last_ns.description: Time of the last payload byte of any stream.

RemoteRunState.description: State of a run another peer drives against this hub (`HubEvent::RemoteRun`).

oneOf.description: `prepare` accepted; this device is being measured.

ResourceStats.description:
CPU and memory of one side over the measurement window (§7.4).

CPU percentages use 100 = one logical CPU, so they can exceed 100.

cpu_ms.description: Process CPU time (user + sys) in the window, ms.

cpu_pct_max.description: Max over 500 ms intervals (priming interval discarded).

sidecar_cpu_pct_max.description: Sidecar max CPU % over 500 ms intervals.

combined.description: Same-process topology: the process plus both sidecars.

peer.description: Peer reference: device name, ULID, tailscale id, hostname or IP.

suite_id.description: Set when the run belongs to a suite.

oneOf.description: Cancelled by the user or a peer.

build_profile.description: `debug` if either side is debug, `unknown` if not recorded, else `release`.

flags.description:
History flags derived from the report, in this order when present:
`debug` (either side a debug build), `overlap` (shared the machine
with other runs), `rate-not-achieved` (the sender could not sustain
its target), `imported`, `same-host`, `same-process`, `mixed-path`,
`partial` (a failed or cancelled run that kept partial results). See
[`RunReport::flags`](crate::report::RunReport::flags).

mode.description:
The workload's mode (`params.mode`: `throughput`, `latency`, `echo`,
`rr`, `pingpong`, …), or `None` for a workload without modes. The app
picks the latest run of the mode its form is in from this.

Series.description: A time series for a chart.

points.description: `[t_ms, value]` pairs, t in the initiator's run timebase.

failed.description: Items whose run did not end `ok`.

value.description: Value; `None` when it could not be measured.

final_echo_ms.description:

lagged.description: Σ `Lagged(n)` on this side's store subscription.

limit_found.description:
Whether the ramp reached a limit: a step lost more than 2% or missed
its rate (or the live loss stop fired). When false, the summary's
`max_sustainable_mbps` is left empty, so a duration-bound ceiling is
never trended as a capacity.

loss_locality.description: usermetrics loss locality, when both sides had usermetrics.

max_burst_datagrams.description: Largest number of datagrams the pacer released back to back.

max_sustainable_mbps.description:
The last step's rate with loss ≤ 2%. When `limit_found` is false this
is only a lower bound: the run ended before any step lost more than
2% or missed its rate.

pacer_late_ms_mean.description: Mean timer lateness of the sender's pacing sleeps, ms.

end_ms.description: End, ms since the sender started.

loss_pct.description: Exact loss of its seq range (filled from the receiver).

offered_mbps.description: What the sender offered during the step, Mb/s.

start_ms.description: Start, ms since the sender started.

sustained.description:

loss stop cut short.
